name: Text Input
summary: A text input is a native `<input>` with a visible label. Use it for any single line of typed text. Three attributes decide how usable it is — `type` and `inputmode` choose the on-screen keyboard, and `autocomplete` is what lets a password manager or an autofill tool complete the form for someone who cannot type it.
demoNote: No JavaScript on this page. A text input that needs a script to be accessible is a broken one. Open it on a phone: each field brings up a different keyboard, and that is the type attribute doing it.

contract.useWhen: A text field, with the type and autocomplete that make it fillable.
keyboard: native: nothing here needs a key handler
states: invalid — aria-invalid=true on the control, set only while the error shows
failureModes: no autocomplete — SC 1.3.5, and the most-skipped criterion in this group
a placeholder standing in for the label, gone the moment anyone types
type=text for an email or a phone number, so the phone keyboard is the wrong one
aria-label instead of a visible label, which find-in-page and translation never see
